claims.summary: Ingress message router that receives a single incoming message and distributes it to one of five directional output paths based on decoded destination.
claims.subject: routeMsg
claims.explanation: The module has one event input i_drive with a 51-bit payload i_msg_51, and five event outputs o_driveEArb/LArb/NArb/SArb/WArb each with a 51-bit data output. The internal flow uses a receiveFifo, a conditional fork (dirFork), per-direction delay elements, and per-direction sendFifos. The assign dependencies show directional valid signals (w_eastVld, w_westVld, w_northVld, w_southVld, w_localVld) that are derived from priority arbitration logic, with localVld being the default when no other direction is valid. This matches a router that decodes a destination field from the message and routes accordingly.

claims.summary: Receives one message, decodes its destination, and forwards it to the correct directional output after buffering and arbitration handshake.
claims.subject: message routing and distribution
claims.explanation: The single input i_drive with payload i_msg_51 enters receiveFifo, then passes through a delay element (delayUart0) to dirFork. The dirFork uses directional valid signals (w_eastVld, w_westVld, w_northVld, w_southVld, w_localVld) to select one of five output paths. Each path has a per-direction delay (delayE/L/N/S/W) and a sendFifo (eastSendFifo etc.) that produces the final o_drive*Arb event. The free signals (i_free*Arb) flow back from the arbiter to each sendFifo, and the receiveFifo produces o_free. The assign dependencies show priority: east/west have highest priority, then north/south (conditional on no east/west), and local is the fallback.

claims.subject: dirFork (cCondFork5)
claims.summary: Conditional 5-way fork that selects the output direction based on decoded destination valid signals.
claims.explanation: dirFork receives the delayed drive event from receiveFifo via delayUart0. It has five conditional outputs (o_driveNext0-4) that connect to per-direction delays. The valid signals w_eastVld, w_westVld, w_northVld, w_southVld, and w_localVld control which output fires. The assign dependencies show w_localVld is the default when no other direction is valid, implementing a priority encoder. The two assign_related connections (westToEast.o_msgVld -> dirFork.valid1 for w_eastVld, eastToWest.o_msgVld -> dirFork.valid0 for w_westVld) suggest the valid signals come from external direction decoders.

claims.subject: receiveFifo (cFifo1)
claims.summary: Input buffer that decouples the incoming message from the routing pipeline.
claims.explanation: receiveFifo receives the i_drive event and its associated payload i_msg_51. It outputs the drive event to the routing pipeline via w_driveFork. It also produces the o_free signal, indicating when the fifo has space for the next message. This provides flow control back to the sender.

claims.subject: per-direction sendFifos (eastSendFifo, localSendFifo, northSendFifo, southSendFifo, westSendFifo)
claims.summary: Output buffers for each direction that decouple the routing pipeline from the downstream arbiter.
claims.explanation: Each sendFifo receives a drive event from its corresponding delay element (e.g., w_driveEFifo for east). It outputs the o_drive*Arb event to the external arbiter. The i_free*Arb input from the arbiter indicates when the fifo can accept the next message, providing backpressure.

claims.subject: w_northVld, w_southVld, w_localVld
claims.summary: Priority arbitration logic for directional valid signals.
claims.explanation: Assignments 6, 8, and 9 implement a priority encoder. w_northVld is asserted when w_northVldSN is true AND neither w_eastVld nor w_westVld is asserted. w_southVld follows the same pattern with w_southVldNS. w_localVld is the default, asserted only when no other direction (west, east, south, north) is valid. This establishes a priority order: east/west > north/south > local.

claims.subject: o_westMsg_51, o_localMsg_51, o_eastMsg_51, o_northMsg_51, o_southMsg_51
claims.summary: Output message payloads driven from internal registered signals.
claims.explanation: Assignments 16-20 show that each directional output message (o_*Msg_51) is driven by a corresponding registered signal (r_*Msg_51). This indicates the message payload is registered before being sent to the output, providing a pipeline stage.

claims.summary: Single message input with bundled payload and flow control.
claims.subject: i_drive / i_msg_51 input pair
claims.explanation: The i_drive event carries the 51-bit message payload i_msg_51. The receiveFifo provides o_free backpressure. This is a standard push interface where the sender asserts i_drive when i_msg_51 is valid, and the receiver asserts o_free when it can accept.

claims.summary: Five directional output interfaces, each with a push event, payload, and backpressure.
claims.subject: o_drive*Arb / o_*Msg_51 output pairs with i_free*Arb backpressure
claims.explanation: Each direction (east, local, north, south, west) has an output event o_drive*Arb, a 51-bit data output o_*Msg_51, and a free input i_free*Arb. The sendFifo asserts o_drive*Arb when it has a message, and the downstream arbiter asserts i_free*Arb when it can accept. This is a standard push interface with backpressure.
